html:
Scipio Aemilianus was the Roman general who destroyed Carthage in 146 BCE and Numantia in Spain in 133 BCE, and a leading statesman of the Roman Republic in its last calm years.

He was born a son of Aemilius Paullus, the victor at Pydna, and adopted into the family of Scipio Africanus, conqueror of Hannibal. As a young man he befriended the Greek hostage Polybius, who became his teacher and later his historian. His circle took up Greek learning and supported writers such as the playwright Terence.

  • Elected consul in 147 BCE though too young, he took charge of the siege of Carthage. The city fell in 146 and was razed. Polybius, who stood beside him, says Scipio wept and quoted Homer on the fall of Troy, fearing Rome would one day meet the same fate. See Rome destroys Carthage and Corinth.
  • Consul again in 134, he restored discipline to the army in Spain and starved Numantia into surrender, ending the Numantine War. The young Gaius Marius served under him.

He married Sempronia, daughter of Cornelia and sister of the Gracchi brothers, but he opposed their land reforms. In 129 he was found dead in his bed, and rumours of murder were never settled. Cicero's On the Republic is set in his garden in that year.
